title: Local acyclicity for an abelian etale sheaf
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] set $\bar s=f\bar x$. Write $X_{(\bar x)}$ and $S_{(\bar s)}$ for the strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with their structural maps to $X$ and $S$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]; the map $X_{(\bar x)}\to S_{(\bar s)}$ is induced by pulling pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ back along $f$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3)-(4). For any geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S_{(\bar s)}$, put
$$V_{f,\bar x,\bar t}=X_{(\bar x)}\times_{S_{(\bar s)}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'$$
(the fibre product of [def-pc-fibre-product]). For any scheme mapping to $X$, write $G|_Y$ for its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Consider the canonical homomorphism
$$\alpha_{G,\bar x,\bar t}:G_{\bar x}\longrightarrow H^0(V_{f,\bar x,\bar t},G|_{V_{f,\bar x,\bar t}})$$
The strict-local ring is strictly henselian and $\bar x$ lifts to its closed point by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). Define this map by the inverse of the germ isomorphism $\Gamma(X_{(\bar x)},G|_{X_{(\bar x)}})\cong G_{\bar x}$ [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk; lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], followed by restriction of global sections to $V_{f,\bar x,\bar t}$. Here stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and $H^q$ is etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], with $H^0=\Gamma$.
Say that $f$ is locally acyclic at $\bar x$ relative to $G$ if, for every such $\bar t$, $\alpha_{G,\bar x,\bar t}$ is an isomorphism and $H^q(V_{f,\bar x,\bar t},G|_{V_{f,\bar x,\bar t}})=0$ for every $q>0$. Say that $f$ is locally acyclic relative to $G$ if this holds at every $\bar x$. Say simply that $f$ is locally acyclic if at every $\bar x$ it is locally acyclic relative to the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] for each positive integer $n$ prime to the characteristic of the residue field at $\bar x$ [def-weil-residue-field] (all positive $n$ in characteristic zero). Say that $f$ is universally locally acyclic if every base change $X\times_S S'\to S'$ along any scheme morphism $S'\to S$ is locally acyclic. No algebraicity condition on $\Omega'$ over the residue field of its image is imposed.

proof.text: For the canonical residue-field algebra structures on Ω supplied by the geometric points x and x ≫ f, apply strictHenselizationResidue to obtain local ring structures and the pointed residue identifications σX and σS.

The field-valued lifts defined by σX and σS equal Spec of strictHenselizationPointEvaluation: their composites with each affine pointed-neighbourhood leg agree by the pointed factorization equations, and the strict-henselization limit makes them equal.

Apply strictHenselizationFunctoriality to f and x. Spec of the resulting coordinate-ring map commutes with the structural morphisms. Its residue compatibility, the preceding lift identifications and contravariant functoriality of Spec give the required pointed equation.

For any second map with the same two equations, compose both maps with each target affine pointed-neighbourhood leg. These composites have the same base map by strictHenselizationStructuralMap_eq and agree at the field-valued closed point by the pointed equations. Etale pointed-map rigidity identifies each pair. The limit hom_ext then identifies the original maps, proving unique existence.

Use the general pointed-section-cone restriction on strictLocalSectionCone, the existing exact-sections instance for the small colimit model, and the general exact-global-sections Leray comparison wherever the former specialized restriction API was used. The cone restriction has the same section formulas, its germ predicate is definitionally identical, and uniqueness identifies the chosen stalk maps. All other argument steps and all scheme models stay as before.
